prompt:
I need the front end for Sproutbox. A free, hugely popular browser coding playground where millions of beginners and hobbyists build small web pages and games, alone or together with friends.

Who's using it: Keisha Moran, 29, a dental hygienist who learned a little JavaScript from Sproutbox tutorials last year. She runs a page for her eight-friend fantasy football league that calculates weekly standings with the league's quirky house scoring rules. She is not a professional programmer and mostly copies and adapts snippets.

What they're doing right now: It's Wednesday on her lunch break. The standings page has shown everyone at zero points since last night. Two of her friends, Dev and Lucía, have edit access, and one of them evidently changed the scoring code. Dev is currently in the project too, apparently poking at it. She wants to find out what changed since Monday and who changed it, and to roll back just the broken part without losing Lucía's new team logos. She also wants to decide whether Dev should keep edit rights or be switched to view-only until the season ends.

What's in the system at this point: Project 'Gridiron Grudge Match Standings' has 6 files: index.html, style.css, scoring.js, teams.json, logos/ (8 PNGs), and README.md. There are 4 people on the project: Keisha (owner), Dev Patel (editor, currently active, last edited scoring.js 3 minutes ago), Lucía Ferraro (editor, last active Tuesday 9:14 pm) and Grant O. (viewer). The history holds 31 saved edits since Monday 8:00 am, each with an author, a time, the files touched and line counts (for example, scoring.js +12/−40 by Dev on Tuesday 11:02 pm). There are 3 comments, one from Lucía on teams.json: 'swapped in the new logos, hope that's ok!' The public page has had 214 views this week. The league's house rules include defensive touchdowns at 9 points and a −3 penalty for the commissioner's team.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
